name: Durotar
summary: Durotar is red canyon country, where young orcs and Darkspear trolls prove themselves to the New Horde. Warchief Thrall founded this dry homeland after the Third War, and named it for his father, Durotan. The Southfury River and the Great Sea hem it in. Razor Hill and the warrior city of Orgrimmar rise from its rock. But quilboar tribes still hold out here, and so do stranded Alliance troops.

sections.title: A Harsh New Home
sections.body: Thrall chose this hard frontier on purpose. Here the orcs would earn an honest living by labor and grit, and not by conquest. The cracked red soil and the towering spires remind them of Draenor, before its ruin. Water is scarce and little of the land can be farmed, yet the Horde has embraced its stark grandeur. Durotar is proof that the orcs have forged their own destiny.

sections.title: Enemies on the Frontier
sections.body: The Horde holds Durotar, but keeping it is still a war. The Razormane quilboar, pushed out when the nation was founded, raid its farms from the western crags. In the south, what is left of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet still holds Tiragarde Keep, and refuses to surrender. Worse still, the demon cult of the Burning Blade lurks in hidden ravines and deep sea caves. It tempts young orcs back to fel power.

sections.title: The Trials of the Darkspear
sections.body: On the southern coast lies Sen'jin Village, where the exiled Darkspear trolls gather under Master Gadrin. Their home was on the nearby Echo Isles. But the witch doctor Zalazane went mad, and with dark voodoo he enslaved his own kin. The Darkspear cannot take the islands back alone. They are counting on new warriors from the Valley of Trials, to break Zalazane's hold.

faq.q: Why did Thrall settle the Horde in such a barren desert?
faq.answer: Thrall chose this unforgiving territory intentionally. After leading the orcs across the Great Sea to Kalimdor, he settled them here. The red earth and rugged mesas reminded the orcs of their ancestral world of Draenor, while its harsh conditions served as penance and a forge for discipline. They embraced the land’s natural defenses. Thrall believed his people needed to earn their survival through honest hardship rather than claiming fertile lands by conquest, ensuring they would not slide back into bloodthirsty complacency. The Barrens lay across the Southfury to the west, and the ruined wilds of Azshara lay to the north.

The land was named in honor of Durotan, Thrall's late father and the former chieftain of the Frostwolf clan. Durotan had opposed the demonic corruption of the orcish clans and was murdered on the orders of the warlock Gul'dan.

faq.q: Why are there human soldiers inside Tiragarde Keep?
faq.answer: The soldiers at Tiragarde Keep are surviving Kul Tiran marines under Lieutenant Benedict, left over from Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's invasion fleet. They hold the crumbling garrison. Even after Proudmoore was slain, these troops refused to surrender or withdraw, maintaining an entrenched hostile outpost right on Durotar's southern coast.

faq.q: What is the conflict on the Echo Isles?
faq.answer: The Darkspear trolls originally established their Kalimdor home on the Echo Isles. However, a powerful witch doctor named Zalazane succumbed to madness and turned his dark magic against his brethren, enslaving their minds. The Darkspear lost their home as a result. The survivors fled to the mainland to establish Sen'jin Village, from which they launch raids to break his hold.

faq.q: What is the Burning Blade doing in Durotar?
faq.answer: The Burning Blade is a subversive demonic cult loyal to the Shadow Council and the Burning Legion. Operatives lurk in secluded spots like Skull Rock and the Burning Blade Coven, attempting to undermine Thrall's leadership and tempt impressionable orcs back into demonic servitude.

faq.q: What connects Durotar to other regions?
faq.answer: A bridge over the Southfury River leads west into the Barrens, while the ruined wilds of Azshara lie to the north. Outside Orgrimmar, a zeppelin tower provides transcontinental air travel directly to Tirisfal Glades and Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.

angles.text: Durotar is your people's new promised land, won through sweat and blood after years of demonic lethargy and internment. Proving your worth in the Valley of Trials is the first rite of passage for every new champion of the Horde.

After escaping the sea witch in the Great Sea, the Darkspear found refuge alongside Thrall in Durotar, but the traitor Zalazane took the Echo Isles from within. Retaking the isles and defending Sen'jin Village is personal.

Durotar is the beating heart of the Horde's military strength. Any Alliance traveler found wandering its sun-scorched canyons will be hunted down on sight by aggressive patrols and native beasts alike.
As a young shaman, you find the arid land alive with raw elemental spirits. You visit sacred sites like the Spirit Rock and the Shrine of the Dormant Flame to attune yourself to earth and fire.
Thrall strictly polices dark magic, forcing the Shadow Council's covens into hiding within places like Skull Rock and beneath the city in the winding caverns of Ragefire Chasm.
